transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Lately I keep thinking about death, and I’m starting to worry about the thoughts I’m having about not wanting to be here anymore. It's really starting to scare me, which is why I decided I needed to come in and talk to someone.
Have you been feeling this way for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two years, or is this a more recent change that has lasted for a few weeks or months?

It’s more of a recent change that’s been going on for about three weeks now. It started right after I found out I failed a key certification exam, and it has been weighing on me constantly ever since without really letting up.
Over these past three weeks, have you lost interest in activities you usually enjoy, or have you noticed a significant change in your appetite or energy levels?

Yes, over these past three weeks I've completely lost interest in painting and salsa dancing because it just feels too exhausting and pointless. My appetite is also gone; I barely eat anything during my 12-hour shifts, and even my mom's homemade food just sits in the fridge because everything tastes like cardboard.

How significantly are these feelings impacting your ability to function at work or in your daily life—are you still able to perform your job duties, or have you become unable to carry out most of your normal activities?

It’s having a huge impact; I’ve been making more charting errors at the clinic, and I had to postpone signing up for my next certification exam because I just can't keep up with the studying. On top of that, I’ve been dodging calls and invites from my friends and family because I simply don't have the energy to show up for anyone anymore.
Have you experienced any moments where you felt completely unable to move or speak, or have you noticed any changes in your perception, such as hearing or seeing things that aren't actually there?

No, I haven't seen or heard things that aren't there, and I haven't been completely unable to move or speak. But I do feel extremely slowed down physically and mentally, like I'm wading through mud when I'm walking or charting at the clinic. It even takes me a really long time just to process and answer simple questions.

In the past few weeks, have you been able to experience any moments of pleasure or temporary mood improvement when something positive happens, or is your mood consistently low and unresponsive to your surroundings?

No, my mood is consistently low and doesn't lift at all, even when something positive happens. I wake up every day with this heavy, hollow feeling in my chest, and nothing seems to bring me any pleasure anymore. Even the things I used to love, like painting or going out with my friends, don't do anything to cheer me up.

Beyond the physical slowing you described, have you noticed any other physical symptoms like waking up much earlier than usual, or does the intensity of your low mood feel significantly worse specifically in the mornings?
I haven't really noticed waking up much earlier than usual. My mood also doesn't feel significantly worse specifically in the mornings; it's just a constant, heavy feeling that stays with me all day.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets criteria for a major depressive episode of moderate severity. She exhibits core symptoms of depressed mood, anhedonia, and fatigue, accompanied by cognitive impairment (charting errors) and psychomotor retardation. F32.2 (severe) is less likely because she does not report the extreme vegetative symptoms or complete inability to function often associated with severe depression, nor the specific morning worsening of mood characteristic of melancholic features.
